qs.q: A 58-year-old man with metastatic pancreatic cancer develops recurrent superficial migratory thrombophlebitis in his lower extremities. Which biological property of this malignancy most directly mediates this hypercoagulable state?
o: Release of tumor-derived tissue factor and mucins
Direct compression of deep pelvic veins by tumor
Stimulation of hepatic clotting factor production
Paraneoplastic secretion of recombinant protein C
qs.e: Tumor cell release of tissue factor and mucins activates the coagulation cascade, causing Trousseau syndrome.
qs.s: Weekly Year 5: ENT Exam - October 30, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A 68-year-old man presents with deep vein thrombosis and migratory superficial thrombophlebitis associated with a newly diagnosed pancreatic malignancy. What is the classic eponym for this finding?
qs.e: Migratory thrombophlebitis and deep vein thrombosis associated with visceral malignancies such as pancreatic cancer is known as Trousseau's sign. Courvoisier's law relates to a palpable non-tender gallbladder in painless jaundice.
qs.s: Pancreatic Head Cancer and Periampullary Tumours: Whipple Procedure: MCQs

qs.q: A 59-year-old man with advanced gastric cancer is noted to have migratory thrombophlebitis during his hospital admission. What is the established name for this paraneoplastic vascular sign?
qs.e: Trousseau's sign is migratory thrombophlebitis, which can occur as a paraneoplastic manifestation in gastrointestinal malignancies such as gastric and pancreatic cancer. Troisier's sign refers to a palpable left supraclavicular lymph node.
qs.s: Gastric Cancer: Presentation, Staging and Gastrectomy: MCQs

qs.q: A patient with an advanced, neglected visceral malignancy presents with recurrent thrombophlebitis affecting multiple, distinct venous sites over a short period. This clinical phenomenon is most strongly linked to which of the following?
o: Severe mechanical compression by lymph nodes
Bacterial colonization of the vessel walls
qs.e: Migratory thrombophlebitis, or Trousseau syndrome, involves repeated thrombophlebitis at different sites and is associated with occult visceral malignancies like pancreatic or lung carcinomas due to tumour-derived mucins and procoagulants. Phlebothrombosis and thrombophlebitis together account for at least 90% of clinical venous disease.

qs.q: A 58-year-old male presents with recurrent migratory thrombophlebitis affecting sequential veins in his arms and legs over the past three months. Which underlying condition should be urgently investigated?
qs.e: Migratory thrombophlebitis, known as Trousseau syndrome, is a hypercoagulable state strongly linked to underlying visceral adenocarcinomas like pancreatic cancer. Factor V Leiden typically causes deep venous thrombosis rather than recurrent migratory superficial thrombophlebitis.

qs.q: A patient with advanced pancreatic cancer develops migratory thrombophlebitis, a hypercoagulable state known as Trousseau syndrome. This condition is most characteristically associated with which tumor?
qs.e: Trousseau syndrome, or migratory thrombophlebitis, is associated with tumor hypercoagulability seen in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. Benign lesions like serous cystadenomas do not typically present with systemic paraneoplastic clotting disorders.
qs.s: Pancreatic Disorders: A Comprehensive Review: MCQs

qs.q: What is the name for recurrent migratory superficial thrombophlebitis in pancreatic cancer?
qs.e: Trousseau syndrome (migratory thrombophlebitis) is a classic paraneoplastic manifestation of procoagulants released by pancreatic and lung adenocarcinomas.
qs.s: Weekly Pathology Exam - March 7, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: A patient with pancreatic cancer develops recurrent migratory superficial thrombophlebitis. What is this paraneoplastic phenomenon called?
qs.e: Trousseau syndrome is migratory thrombophlebitis due to tumor-associated hypercoagulability, classic for PDAC.
